Article Title: Manipur violence: 306 killed, 49 missing since May 2023
Article Text:
Manipur violence leaves several dead since 2023

Violence erupted over ST status demand

President’s Rule revoked earlier this year

At least 306 people have been killed and 49 remain missing in the ethnic violence that broke out in Manipur in May 2023, state home minister Govindas Konthoujam told the Assembly on Thursday.Responding to a query by BJP MLA Sapam Ranjan Singh on the second day of the ongoing Assembly session, Konthoujam said the figures were recorded as of August 31, 2026.“Since the violence started on May 3, 2023, 306 people have died, and 49 people are still missing as of August 31, 2026,” he said.The ethnic clashes between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities began on May 3, 2023, after a ‘Tribal Solidarity March’ was organised in the hill districts to protest the Meitei community’s demand for Scheduled Tribe status.Meiteis account for around 53 per cent of Manipur’s population and live mainly in the Imphal Valley, while tribals, including Nagas and Kukis, constitute around 40 per cent and reside predominantly in the hill districts.The prolonged violence resulted in widespread displacement and triggered significant political developments in the state.President’s Rule was imposed in Manipur on February 13, 2025, after then chief minister N Biren Singh resigned amid the prolonged ethnic conflict. The 60-member Assembly was subsequently placed under suspended animation.President’s Rule was revoked on February 4, 2026, paving the way for the formation of a new government under BJP leader Yumnam Khemchand Singh as chief minister.
Article Summary: Violence erupted over the Meitei community’s demand for Scheduled Tribe status. The prolonged violence resulted in widespread displacement and triggered significant political developments in the state. At least 306 people have been killed and 49 remain missing in the ethnic violence that broke out in May 2023.

Article Title: More teachers, better access, fewer pupils: India’s government school paradox
Article Text:
Gujarat Government school

From buffaloes and buckets to what the national numbers say

Nearly 1 lakh fewer govt schools, but access improves on paper

Nearly 1 lakh less government school in 10 years

Govt schools are losing pupils even as the system improves

Drop-outs decreasing

Digital access surges, but TOI finds a different classroom reality

Toilets on paper, TOI finds the functionality gap on the ground

The basic-access gap remains

Basic access gap remains

Schools are back in focus. In larger policy discussions and political debates. The Opposition, emboldened by its NEET protest victory, is looking to up the ante by exposing ramshackle school infrastructure in different states, starting with Rajasthan. TOI ground reports, too, have found gross inadequacies in government schools across different parts of the state. Particularly jarring is the fact that in Kota , widely called the coaching capital of India, many government schools are in a dilapidated state. wider ground report by TOI reporters across the country found that Rajasthan was hardly an outlier. In Bihar, nearly 200 children from four classes were sharing a single room at one school while cattle occupied two others. In Uttarakhand, leaking roofs meant buckets and umbrellas had become classroom fixtures. In Madhya Pradesh, TOI found schools struggling with teacher shortages and unsafe buildings. Keralam was a prominent exception to this broader picture.However, the fact remains that in a country of 1.4 billion people, structural gaps are perhaps expected, if certainly not desired. A good metric of how much the school system has improved over the years is to look at the data furnished by the central government and its allied agencies.The pan-India numbers make for interesting reading. Rajasthan had 7,200 single-teacher schools in 2025-26, while only 36.4% of schools reported ramps with handrails and 26.3% had toilets tailored for Children with Special Needs (CwSN).The country has nearly a lakh fewer government schools than it did a decade ago, and those schools are losing pupils. It also has more teachers, far fewer children in single-teacher schools, more teenagers reaching higher secondary and internet access in about two-thirds of schools. Fewer than half of schools, however, report a toilet designed for children with special needs. Yet despite improvements in many metrics, government-school enrolment is falling.Most of what is known about India's schools comes from UDISE+, the Unified District Information System for Education Plus. It is an annual, census-like administrative database covering schools across management types. Schools report on their pupils, teachers and infrastructure, from enrolment and staffing to toilets, electricity, ramps, computers and internet access, and they are incorporated into the Union education ministry's national school statistics.The system grew out of UDISE, created in 2012-13 by merging separate elementary and secondary databases. UDISE+ became its online successor from 2018-19. The government uses it to locate infrastructure gaps, and states draw on it when seeking support for classrooms, toilets, drinking water, electricity, libraries and digital facilities under schemes such as Samagra Shiksha.A school can figure in the database as open and equipped with a particular facility, but reality can be very different. TOI's visits across states repeatedly brought out that distinction.India had 11,04,796 government schools in 2015-16. Ten years later, UDISE+ records 10,05,245, a difference of 99,551 schools or 9%. The rider is that a school leaving the UDISE count can reflect closure, merger, rationalisation, reclassification or other administrative change.The decline is stark in some states. Madhya Pradesh had 1,21,976 government schools in 2015-16; by 2025-26 the count was 91,199, a reduction of 30,777. Uttar Pradesh fell from 1,62,645 to 1,37,103, a reduction of 25,542. Together, the two states account for about 56.6% of the national net decline over the decade.There have also been changes in school mapping and verification, with UDISE+ replacing the older UDISE system from 2018-19. Questioned in Parliament, the Centre has said that decisions on opening, closing and rationalising schools lie largely with states and Union territories, while the Right to Education framework requires elementary schools to remain accessible within prescribed neighbourhood limits.Between 2018-19 and 2024-25, the Gross Access Ratio rose from 88.24% to 95.35% at the secondary level and from 65.05% to 94.97% at higher secondary. GAR measures the proportion of habitations or villages with a school available within the prescribed distance; it is not an enrolment ratio. So although there are fewer schools, the measured access ratio has improved. This is also part of the government's defence.Government-school enrolment fell from 12.75 crore in 2023-24 to 11.89 crore in 2025-26, nearly 85.9 lakh fewer pupils in just two years, a decline of 6.7%. Over the same period, enrolment in private unaided schools rose from 9.00 crore to 9.89 crore, an increase of about 88.3 lakh, or 9.8%. The thinning out is also visible over a decade with average enrolment per government school falling from about 132 pupils in 2014-15 to 120 in 2024-25, a decline of roughly 9%; the latest UDISE+ figures put it at about 118 in 2025-26.One figure from the government's own parliamentary reply captures the scale of it. In 2024-25, government institutions accounted for 68.9% of all schools in India but 49.2% of all enrolment.A movement this large might be expected to have triggered a substantial investigation. On July 29, 2026, the government was asked why government-school enrolment had fallen from about 12.8 crore to 11.9 crore while private enrolment rose from around 9 crore to 9.9 crore.The ministry confirmed the numbers but did not cite or summarise such an assessment in its reply. Instead, it listed the interventions being made to strengthen government education.NITI Aayog's 2026 UDISE+-based review says the broader decline in enrolment through 2024-25 is partly attributable to demographic shifts, particularly falling fertility and a smaller school-age population, alongside school consolidation and challenges in retaining pupils at higher levels.Ranabir Bhattacharyya, teacher-in-charge of the English-medium primary section of Chetla Boys' High School in Kolkata, points to some of the practical issues with UDISE+ and also offers context for the dwindling numbers. He says the data had many issues at one point, but the pipeline has increasingly been made more robust as the government seeks to bring all students onto the platform to roll out various developmental schemes aimed at schoolchildren.He alleges that there was earlier an incentive in certain quarters to inflate pupil numbers, but says tighter vigilance has reduced that tendency and the numbers now being reflected are closer to reality. Ranabir, however, flags other problems like the website can be difficult to use and often suffers technical glitches, while the absence of additional staff increases the workload of those responsible for keeping the data updated. As a result, underreporting can happen too, according to him.India had 96.96 lakh teachers in 2020-21 and 102.73 lakh in 2025-26, nearly 5.77 lakh additional teachers in five years. Single-teacher schools fell from 1,10,971 in 2023-24 to 1,00,843 in 2025-26, and the number of children enrolled in them dropped more steeply still, from 39.94 lakh to 29.12 lakh. Nearly 11 lakh fewer children are now in such schools.But the national improvement hides striking state differences. Andhra Pradesh alone has 16,357 single-teacher schools; Jharkhand has 9,827, Maharashtra 9,269, Karnataka 8,042 and Uttar Pradesh 7,874. Those five states together account for just over half of India's 1,00,843 single-teacher schools.And this is one area where the statistical picture intersects sharply with what TOI reporters saw. In Madhya Pradesh, TOI found 70 children and one teacher operating from a single dilapidated room at a school in Bhopal's Kolar, while students in Classes XI and XII at a PM SHRI school in Mandla had gone without teachers for newly introduced streams for a year.Uttarakhand has 2,655 single-teacher schools, about 11.8% of its entire school network, alongside its unusually high proportion of very small schools. The Centre acknowledges the problem. It has told Parliament that recruitment and postings are primarily state responsibilities; and that it repeatedly presses states on faster recruitment and redeployment while supporting them under Samagra Shiksha.Ranabir highlights another issue involving children of migrant labourers. He says that when a student shifts from one school to another, the subsequent UDISE+ entry does not always move smoothly as it requires manual intervention. West Bengal School Education Minister Dipak Barman, speaking to TOI, says many private schools in the state have not uploaded their student lists. Barman says the state is working to get the figures updated. It is hard to know whether similar anomalies exist elsewhere, but if they do, they could significantly undermine the purpose of what the central government is trying to achieve with the UDISE+ platform.The encouraging part is that reported dropout rates are falling. In many states, girl students are incentivised to continue school education. At the same time, higher-secondary Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) rose from 56.2% in 2023-24 to 61.7% in 2025-26, and the secondary dropout rate fell from 14.1% to 9.5% over the same period. Here too, the national number hides enormous variation. Keralam, for instance, reported secondary retention of 99.1% in 2025-26.For many from financially weaker sections, there is a significant opportunity cost to staying in school after Class X. The government has therefore deployed a range of measures to keep more students in the system. Parliamentary replies point to PM POSHAN, residential schools and hostels, KGBVs, transport assistance, free textbooks and uniforms, enrolment campaigns and vocational education, and more recently to Vidya Samiksha Kendras and APAAR IDs as tools for tracking students who drop out or move between schools.In step with the government's Digital India push, digital infrastructure has expanded rapidly. In 2020-21, 24.5% of schools reported internet access; by 2025-26, 67.4% did. Computer availability rose from 41.3% to 69.9%. The approved budget for ICT labs, smart classrooms and other digital initiatives rose from ₹381.1 crore in 2018-19 to ₹3,221.1 crore in 2025-26.NITI Aayog's 2026 UDISE+-based analysis of functional smart classrooms shows coverage rising from 14.9% of schools in 2021-22 to 30.6% in 2024-25. In other words, even after rapid expansion, nearly seven in ten schools still lacked one.The interstate divide is striking. Punjab reported functional smart classrooms in 80.1% of schools and Delhi in 75.7%; the corresponding figures were only 4.3% in Meghalaya, 5.7% in West Bengal, 14.9% in Bihar and 19.8% in Uttar Pradesh. Tamil Nadu offers the opposite story: its reported coverage went from virtually zero in 2021-22 to 60.8% in 2024-25.TOI's ground visits underline why infrastructure numbers need context. In Uttar Pradesh, schools visited by reporters had toilets and drinking water, but digital resources were missing; in Himachal Pradesh, strong coverage of basic facilities coexisted with substantially weaker smart-classroom and disability-access indicators.Regarding West Bengal's poor showing, Barman says many of the state's UDISE+ figures have not been properly updated and that the government is working to correct them, and is looking to start 2000 smart classrooms in the next one year. He says Bengal expects to be among the top 10 when the next calculation is made.India is now close to universal provision of toilet facilities in schools, at least on paper. UDISE+ reports girls'-toilet availability in 98.5% of girls' and co-educational schools in 2025-26. But availability and functionality are not the same.TOI's ground reporting provides a simple illustration of that distinction. Schools visited in Uttar Pradesh had separate toilets for boys and girls, but reporters found many of them unclean, with teachers blaming the absence of sanitation workers. This issue of not having adequate sanitation staff is something Ranabir also flagged repeatedly.The same NITI Aayog analysis, using 2024-25 data, puts national functional girls'-toilet coverage at 94%, up from 85.17% a decade earlier. Yet the state map remains uneven.In 2024-25, Bihar and Odisha were both at 98.1% functional girls'-toilet coverage and West Bengal at 99.6%, while Rajasthan stood at 87.3%. Meghalaya was at 68.7%, Arunachal Pradesh 73.7% and Manipur 74.5%.In 2020-21, 24.5% of schools reported internet access and 41.3% computers. About 48.3% reported ramps with handrails and 25.3% toilets for children with special needs. By 2025-26, internet availability had reached 67.4% and computers 69.9%. Ramps with handrails were at 58.2%, while CwSN-friendly toilets stood at only 40.1%.The state contrasts are revealing. Himachal Pradesh reports functional electricity in 99.1% of schools and computers in 87.2%, but internet reaches only 66.2% and CwSN-friendly toilets 34%. At the same time, 18.3% of its schools are single-teacher schools and almost half have 30 pupils or fewer.Keralam, the prominent exception in TOI's ground reporting, also stands apart on several UDISE measures. Computer availability is 99.5%, internet access 92.6%, and only 67 schools, about 0.4% of its network, are single-teacher schools. Secondary retention is 99.1%. The state is not without gaps, only around 51.7% of schools report CwSN-friendly toilets but the overall contrast with many other states is striking.The Accessibility Code was notified in 2024, and Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI provide funds for facility upliftment. Ranabir says funds often come in a trickle or are regularly delayed. As a result, he says, many of these metrics do not improve as smoothly as desired. He also highlights that many rural schools have irregular electricity supply, and hence while internet and other digital facilities are present on paper, reality can be different.Taken together, most of these service and outcome indicators have moved positively. Yet government-school enrolment is falling. That may partly reflect an aspirational society where some parents are looking to private schools for stronger English-language exposure, soft skills, peer networks and perceived advantages in college and beyond. Anecdotally, one can also see the mushrooming of English-medium schools in suburbs and mofussils.But the national data do not by themselves establish why families make these choices. Some of the decline may also reflect cleaner data and ironically even lack of proper uploading of data as pointed out by the Bengal education minister.There is no one-size-fits-all solution for such a large country. The data show substantial progress on several fronts, yet the lived reality may be different in some places. For now, the government will need to tick the boxes on what should be absolutely non-negotiable in terms of core deliverables, including the lacunae exposed in those reports. Winning the larger battle for aspiration may be a challenge for another day, or another decade.
Article Summary: India has nearly a lakh fewer government schools than it did a decade ago. It also has more teachers, far fewer children in single-teacher schools, more teenagers reaching higher secondary and internet access in about two-thirds of schools. Fewer than half of schools report a toilet designed for children with special needs.

Article Title: Nalsar row: SC strikes down BCI orders, says it has 'no statutory power to regulate conduct of students'
Article Text:
How the NALSAR row began

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday held that the Bar Council of India has "no statutory authority to regulate the conduct of law students". The court set aside two BCI notifications issued against students of Hyderabad's Nalsar University of Law.A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order.The orders were linked to the students' protest over Chief Justice of India Surya Kant's proposed participation in the university's convocation.The court's observation came after the BCI initially directed state Bar Councils not to enrol Nalsar's 2026 law graduates as advocates following a student campaign opposing CJI Surya Kant's proposed participation as chief guest at the university's convocation.Also read - BCI action, U-turn and SC rebuke: How NALSAR students' protest against CJI kicked up a row The BCI later withdrew the directive and allowed the graduates to be enrolled while an inquiry was pending.The controversy began after several Nalsar students submitted representations asking the university to reconsider its invitation to CJI Surya Kant. The students referred to remarks attributed to the CJI during a hearing concerning alleged police excesses against protesters during a July 20 march to Parliament.At least six representations were submitted by students from different batches, with the first being sent on July 23. The students argued that inviting the CJI was inconsistent with the university's stated commitment to constitutional rights, access to justice and reasoned engagement with grievances.One representation cited the CJI's response to an offer to show videos of the alleged police action: "We are not interested in videos; we don’t have time to watch." It also quoted him as telling counsel: "Don’t waste our time, and don’t waste your time".The students maintained that their objection was rooted in constitutional values and not disrespect towards the judicial office."We respect the CJI’s position. But we have been taught the Constitution and constitutional values, and we don’t want to support something that goes against those values," a student who was also part of the Student bar council had told TOI.The dispute escalated when BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra directed state Bar Councils not to enrol Nalsar's 2026 law graduates as advocates until further orders.The BCI sought a report from Nalsar identifying students who had allegedly initiated, organised or mobilised the campaign against CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation.The council's initial communication stated, “Till further orders, no student of Nalsar University of Law, who has obtained law degree in the year 2026, shall be enrolled by any state bar council as an advocate.”It also said, “A student of Law, having no regard or respect for the highest judicial office of the country, is not expected to be a responsible or sensible advocate, teacher or a judge. Such persons shall always be a liability on the profession. Such conduct reflects adversely upon the person’s suitability for entry into or association with the legal profession and is inconsistent with the dignity, discipline and ethical standards of the legal profession. ”The BCI further alleged that some members of Nalsar's academic staff had been involved in "misleading, instigating and misguiding" students.“As per some reliable sources, there exists groupism and dirty politics among some of the academic staff and they have played a very active role in misleading, instigating and misguiding the students. This is a very serious matter. The teachers, instead of involving themselves in their teaching job, are doing nasty politics in the campus. BCI, being the regulator of Legal Education cannot be a mute spectator of such a serious situation. ”The directive drew criticism from sections of the legal fraternity, with Supreme Court bar association president Vikas Singh describing the move as arbitrary, illegal and disproportionate, while maintaining that he did not support the students' opposition to the CJI's invitation.The BCI withdrew its original directive within hours amid the criticism. In its revised communication, Mishra said the council had “thoroughly discussed and deliberated” on the earlier letter and modified its direction.He said the “vast majority” of Nalsar's 2026 graduating students were innocent and “were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect”. However, he added, “It has been further reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating innocent students.”The revised decision permitted the 2026 graduates to be enrolled while the BCI awaited an inquiry report from Nalsar.
Article Summary: The court set aside two BCI notifications issued against students of Hyderabad's Nalsar University of Law. The orders were linked to the students' protest over Chief Justice of India Surya Kant's proposed participation in the university's convocation. The BCI initially directed state Bar Councils not to enrol NALSar's 2026 law graduates as advocates.

Article Title: TMC alleges 'systematic misuse of police' by BJP in Bengal; writes to President Murmu
Article Text:
TMC MP Derek O'Brien

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress TMC ) on Thursday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu and West Bengal governor RN Ravi, seeking time for party delegations to meet them and highlight the alleged lawlessness in the state.The TMC accused the ruling BJP of “systematically misusing” the West Bengal Police, calling it “disturbing.”"TMC workers are being targeted by the police across the state. Party offices are being vandalised. The police are following no rules. Police are acting openly as BJP cadres. There is utter lawlessness here. In this situation, we have written to the President of India, and the Trinamool Congress has written to the Governor of West Bengal, seeking an urgent appointment of a Trinamool Congress delegation to discuss the disturbing situation in Bengal," the party's Rajya Sabha MP Derek O'Brien told reporters.The development came hours after TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that "BJP hooligans armed with weapons" stormed the party's Camac Street office in Kolkata in the early hours of the day and vandalised the premises, assaulted staff, and damaged electronic equipment."What happened at Camac Street this morning is a disgraceful assault on the rule of law. At around 4.30 am, BJP hooligans, armed with weapons, stormed our party office in the heart of Kolkata.They attacked our people, snatched their phones, smashed furniture, ransacked the premises and destroyed electronic equipment. And where was Kolkata Police? For nearly TWO HOURS, despite repeated calls and emails from our people and lawyers, there was no response. This is outrageous and unacceptable. We demand the immediate arrest of every person involved in this attack," he wrote on X.The Diamond Harbour MP, nephew of TMC supremo and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, asked chief minister Suvendu Adhikari if he was “scared” of the TMC and was therefore resorting to "intimidation."“This is what the BJP has done to my party office in the early hours of this morning. Will the Governor of WB act? Will the Union Home Minister act? Will the PMO act? Or will they continue to look the other way? It is high time the judiciary, particularly the Calcutta High Court, takes serious note of what is happening and acts to uphold the rule of law in West Bengal. And one simple question for Suvendu Adhikari: why are you so scared of the Trinamool Congress and of me that you have to resort to this kind of intimidation? If this is how the Opposition is to be treated in West Bengal, through violence, vandalism and intimidation, then the Chief Minister has no moral authority to remain in office.He must resign. This is not democracy. This is political thuggery... Nothing will be forgotten,” Abhishek Banerjee added.The BJP, meanwhile, rejected Abhishek Banerjee’s allegation of “vendetta”, arguing that if that were the case, no TMC leader would have remained “unscathed” after the party’s defeat in the April assembly elections, which ended its 15-year rule in West Bengal."If the BJP were engaging in vendetta politics, then after the election results were declared, none of the defeated Trinamool Congress MLAs, ministers, and MPs would have remained unscathed... Trinamool members are throwing eggs at each other and vandalising each other's offices. Those who faced injustice at the hands of Abhishek Banerjee, when he was a top party leader, understand the situation," BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said.
Article Summary: The TMC accused the ruling BJP of “systematically misusing” the West Bengal Police. The development came hours after TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that "BJP hooligans armed with weapons" stormed the party's Camac Street office in Kolkata in the early hours of the day.

Article Title: Captain falls ill, IndiGo Doha-BLR flight safely diverts to Muscat
Article Text:
IndiGo flight 6E 1302, operating from Doha to Bengaluru on Sept 3, 2026 was diverted to Muscat due to an urgent requirement of medical attention for one of the operating crew members. The said crew member was attended to by medical team upon landing and is feeling better now.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An IndiGo flight operating from Doha to Bengaluru (6E 1302) was diverted to Muscat after the pilot-in-command (PIC) fell ill. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed in Muscat. The airline is sending another aircraft to Muscat to fly passengers to their destination. The PIC has received medical care and has recovered."IndiGo flight 6E 1302, operating from Doha to Bengaluru on Sept 3, 2026 was diverted to Muscat due to an urgent requirement of medical attention for one of the operating crew members. The said crew member was attended to by medical team upon landing and is feeling better now,” an IndiGo spokesperson said."An alternate aircraft along with a new set of crew has been arranged to continue the journey to Bengaluru. We regret the inconvenience caused to our customers and are making all efforts to minimise it, including offering refreshments and timely updates as they wait for the aircraft at Muscat. The safety of our customers, crew, and aircraft remains our top priority at IndiGo,” the spokesperson added.
Article Summary: IndiGo flight operating from Doha to Bengaluru (6E 1302) was diverted to Muscat after the pilot-in-command (PIC) fell ill. An emergency was declared and the aircraft landed in Muscat. The PIC has received medical care and has recovered. An alternate aircraft along with a new set of crew has been arranged to continue the journey.

Article Title: PM Modi takes stock of flood situation in Varanasi as water crosses warning mark
Article Text:
The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall.PM Modi, who is also the Member of Parliament from Varanasi, sought detailed information from the district magistrate about the river's water level and the arrangements being made at relief camps for people affected by the floods.The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected and ensure that all necessary facilities are made available immediately.He also instructed officials to make immediate arrangements wherever there is an additional requirement for relief material and expedite relief work for affected people.PM Modi further directed the administration to maintain constant vigilance over the flood situation and relief operations and ensure that immediate assistance reaches those affected.The Prime Minister's intervention came as the Ganga continued to rise in Varanasi.According to the Central Water Commission (CWC), the river's water level reached 70.54 metres at the Rajghat gauge site at 6 am on Thursday, crossing the warning level of 70.262 metres. The water level was rising at a rate of 2 cm per hour.The danger level at the site is 71.262 metres, while the highest flood level is 73.901 metres.The district administration has been closely monitoring areas affected by the rising waters of the Ganga and Varuna rivers. On Tuesday, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and Varanasi Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal inspected several flood-affected areas after travelling by an NDRF boat from Namo Ghat.The officials visited Salarpur, Saraiya, Konia, Pul Kohna, Dhelvaria and Sarai Mohana to assess waterlogging and the situation of residents. They also interacted with affected people and assured them of all possible assistance.The district magistrate directed officials to remain on high alert and keep arrangements ready to shift residents to safer locations. He also ordered that boats and other resources remain available for relief and rescue operations.Relief camps at the Primary School in Salarpur and Vidya Vihar Inter College were also inspected. Officials were directed to ensure adequate food, drinking water, electricity, lighting, sanitation, healthcare and security, with special attention to children, women and elderly people.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar. He took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall. The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected.

Article Title: Ex-IAF wing commander Abhinandan Varthaman who shot down Pak jet after Balakot strikes joins private airline
Article Text:
His move to commercial aviation comes after a distinguished career in the IAF

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Indian Air Force Group Captain and Vir Chakra awardee Abhinandan Varthaman has joined Goa-based regional airline FLY91 as a pilot.Varthaman, who became widely known after shooting down a Pakistani fighter during an aerial engagement in 2019 before being captured by Pakistan, joined the airline in August.His move to commercial aviation comes after a distinguished career in the IAF, including his role in the aerial combat that followed India's Balakot air strikes.On February 26, 2019, the IAF carried out an air strike on a Jaish-e-Mohammed facility in Balakot, Pakistan, days after a terrorist attack on a CRPF convoy in Pulwama killed 40 personnel.The following day, Pakistani fighter jets attempted to launch an aerial attack, prompting the IAF to scramble aircraft to intercept them.Varthaman, then a Wing Commander with the Srinagar-based 51 Squadron, was flying a MiG-21 Bison when he engaged a Pakistani F-16. The IAF said he shot down the Pakistani fighter before his own aircraft was hit.Varthaman ejected over territory controlled by Pakistan and was taken into custody by the Pakistani Army. He was released three days later following intense diplomatic and political pressure from India.He was awarded the Vir Chakra, India's third-highest wartime gallantry award, in 2021 for his actions during the aerial engagement. He was subsequently promoted to Group Captain.Also read | Balakot hero Abhinandan Varthaman conferred Vir Chakra

Article Title: Operation Sindoor commander Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra selected as Ram temple Trust’s first CEO
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lucknow: Sixteen months after Operation Sindoor, the officer who commanded India’s western air operations has been chosen for a very different responsibility. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has selected Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as the first Chief Executive Officer of the Ram temple in Ayodhya Speaking to TOI, Mishra said, “I came to know about my appointment via news, I’m yet to receive official communication from trust.”The decorated former Indian Air Force commander retired in April 2026 and will now oversee the temple Trust’s expanding administrative responsibilities. However, the standard operating procedure for the appointment and functioning of the CEO has not yet been finalised, said Govind Dev Giri, general secretary of the Trust.Mishra was the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian Air Force’s Western Air Command when Operation Sindoor was launched on May 7, 2025, in response to the Pahalgam terror attack.Much of the air operations in four days was directed from the command rooms of the Western Air Command, one of the Air Force’s most important operational formations. Mishra oversaw decisions linked to the deployment of aircraft and air defence assets during the military response.Also read | Ram Mandir’s first CEO has a war command pedigree: Meet Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra He was among the senior military commanders recognised for leadership during Operation Sindoor. President Droupadi Murmu conferred the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal on him in recognition of his distinguished service during the operation.Mishra’s appointment brings to the Trust a senior leader with extensive experience in operational planning, coordination, logistics and managing large formations.In a recent podcast interview, Mishra spoke about the air campaign during Operation Sindoor and explained how Indian forces identified and struck targets deep inside Pakistan. He described how a target located around 314 km away was destroyed after a brief operational instruction to “shoot”.While discussing the operation, he highlighted the importance of planning, precision, technology and coordination among different arms of the armed forces. Several operational details, however, remain classified.Mishra has roots in Uttar Pradesh. He originally belongs to Bhopatpura in Deoria district, around three hours by road from Ayodhya. He comes from a middle-class family and his father was a lecturer.Mishra joined the National Defence Academy in 1983 and was commissioned as a fighter pilot in December 1986. He later qualified as an experimental test pilot, one of the most specialised roles in military aviation.During his career, he served as chief test pilot of both the Indian Air Force and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. In the role, he flew aircraft during development and testing stages, assessing their performance and identifying technical limitations before induction and operational deployment.Following the terrorist attack on the Pathankot air base in Jan 2016, Mishra was selected to take over the station and strengthen its administration and security systems. He later commanded the Aircraft and Systems Testing Establishment in Bengaluru, which works with HAL, the Defence Research and Development Organisation and civilian scientists on aviation systems.Mishra also served for three years at Air Headquarters in New Delhi, where he handled defence procurement. He was associated with around 75 projects and led the Air Force’s role in the first emergency procurement tranche during 2019 and 2020. His professional training includes war management at the Air Command and Staff College in the United States and strategic studies at the Royal College of Defence Studies in London.The Trust’s CEO selection process began with 5,585 applications. The selection committee, headed by retired Justice Permod Kohli and comprising Lieutenant General V.K. Chaturvedi and nuclear scientist Dr Suresh Haware, conducted technology-assisted screening, verification and online assessments.The process was coordinated by the Trust secretariat under Sameer Panda.The field was eventually narrowed to 16 candidates, who were interviewed in Ayodhya on Au​g 11 and 12. A panel of three names was submitted to the Trust on Sept 1, following which Mishra was selected.As CEO, Mishra is expected to oversee the temple’s day-to-day administration, pilgrim facilities, financial arrangements, staff coordination and management of major religious events. The Trust will now finalise the CEO’s powers, responsibilities, reporting structure and service conditions before the appointment is formally operationalised.
Article Summary: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has selected Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as the first Chief Executive Officer of the Ram temple in Ayodhya. Mishra was the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian Air Force’s Western Air Command when Operation Sindoor was launched.

Article Title: CBI probe necessary into Disha Salian's death: HC
Article Text:
Bombay HC directed CBI to file an FIR and probe the case thoroughly

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Observing that the June 8, 2020, death of celebrity manager Disha Salian had "many glaring discrepancies" which necessitated proper and substantive investigation, Bombay HC directed CBI to file an FIR and probe the case thoroughly. No one is to be named as an accused without sufficient grounds, HC clarified."Suspicious circumstances'' surrounding the death necessitate the registration of an FIR, HC bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and RR Bhonsale held. But HC said it has "not made any observations against any particular individual"."The police probe raises more questions than it answers. Therefore, an investigation by CBI is necessary.''A delayed spot panchanama nine hours later, on June 9, has “indications that the police were not treating the case as an accidental death case but they were suspecting foul play,’’ the high court observed.HC had last Friday reserved for orders her father’s plea to probe the death as a murder, not suicide or an accident. The father’s counsel, Nilesh Ojha, cited “suspicious circumstances” to seek a proper CBI probe as he argued her death was “the outcome of a deep-rooted conspiracy involving powerful people”.Disha Salian (28) died by suicide and there was no foul play by anyone, the state submitted through its public prosecutor Shishir Hiray.Disha worked briefly with the late film actor Sushant Singh Rajput, who died just days later that month on June 14, aged 34, in his Bandra flat. Her father claimed both deaths were “interlinked”.Interact with the family with sensitivity, HC directed CBI on Wednesday. But simultaneously, “care should be taken that no innocent person is harassed and the offenders, if any, are made to face the trial,’’ the judgement authored by Justice Kotwal said.The father made allegations against Aditya Thackeray of Shiv Sena (UBT). Thackeray intervened and through his senior counsel Sudeep Pasbola said the allegations were “motivated with malafide intentions” to damage his reputation when he is “neither directly nor indirectly connected with any alleged offence.’’ Pasbola expressed sympathy for Disha’s father but said CBI cannot be directed to do a roving inquiry.The ruling made no reference to any names and directed: “Nobody shall be treated as an accused unless in the opinion of the IO there are sufficient gr-ounds to raise reasonable suspicion against him.”The state and Pasbola said the father can file a private complaint before a magistrate for police. HC said with two probes that went on for almost six years, it would be improper to ask Salian to now seek a police probe order from a magistrate. HC said Ojha is right the magistrate has no power to direct CBI to investigate. HC held that police had sufficient opportunity, but didn’t register an FIR to conduct a thorough probe, instead carried on a probe “inadequate and insufficient’’ in the facts of the case.HC clarified, “We have not made any observations against any particular individual. That would be strictly within the realm of the investigation.” Kuldeep Patil, CBI counsel, informed the court that the agency had never thus far probed Disha’s death. Both Hiray and Pasbola said the father can go with a private complaint to a magistrate first.HC, on being shown documents including the panchanama, photographs of the body, and other details from the inquiry, raised questions on various aspects it found “suspicious’’ including whet-her injuries were consistent with a fall from such a height and details regarding clothes.
Article Summary: Bombay HC directed CBI to file an FIR and probe the case thoroughly. No one is to be named as an accused without sufficient grounds, HC clarified. Disha worked briefly with the late film actor Sushant Singh Rajput, who died just days later that month on June 14, aged 34.

Article Title: US reacts to PM Modi-Iran president Pezeshkian meet; issues warning to countries 'helping' Tehran
Article Text:

The US has warned countries against helping Iran evade sanctions, saying those that assist Tehran in generating revenue could themselves face sanctions. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued the warning after Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan.Asked about the PM Modi-Pezeshkian meeting and whether India and Iran were discussing a trade deal, Rubio said, “Well, I don't think there's a trade deal between India and Iran. Obviously there are, you know, countries all develop their own foreign policy, and many countries around the world talk to the Iranian regime.”Rubio acknowledged that several countries maintain contact with Tehran but stressed that Washington would take action against countries that help Iran bypass US sanctions.“No country should be helping Iran evade sanctions. No country should be out there helping them create mechanisms by which they can generate revenue that they will then use to sponsor terrorism and try to build a nuclear weapon,” Rubio said.“And if countries decide to do that, then we're going to have to sanction them, too,” he added.PM Modi's meeting with Pezeshkian came as the Iranian president travelled to Bishkek for the SCO summit, where regional and international issues are expected to dominate discussions.Ahead of his departure, Pezeshkian said Iran did not seek war but would respond “with strength and determination” to any aggression. He also warned that instability in the region would be detrimental to all countries and called for greater cooperation on economic and security issues.“This meeting is very important and most of the leaders of the region will be present in it. In a situation where some international institutions are seeking to create a unified space in the world, this meeting is considered a symbol of the existence of diverse and independent voices in the global arena,” he said.During the meeting with Pezeshkian, Modi is expected to discuss bilateral ties and regional developments. India has consistently called for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve issues in West Asia.PM Modi had also spoken to Pezeshkian in March, when the Iranian president briefed him on developments in the region. PM Modi had stressed India's concerns over the safety of Indian nationals in the region, including Iran, as well as the need for uninterrupted transit of energy and goods.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued the warning after the meeting. He said those that assist Tehran in generating revenue could themselves face sanctions.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay is set to move a resolution in the state assembly on Thursday urging the Centre to recognise Tamil as the principal language of the Madras high court , official sources said.The resolution will be moved by Vijay during the assembly session and is likely to be taken up for discussion. It will seek a formal framework to ensure that judgments, decrees and judicial orders of the high court are also made available in Tamil.The move is expected to highlight Tamil's status as a classical language. It will also point to the significant development of legal terminology in Tamil. The resolution is likely to cite technology-enabled translation facilities as another factor supporting the proposal.The state government will also refer to the existing legal provisions governing the use of regional languages in high court proceedings and judgments. Under the current framework, a state's official language can be used in addition to English, but this requires the Governor's authorisation and the prior consent of the President.The resolution is also expected to recall an earlier attempt by the Tamil Nadu assembly. On December 6, 2006, the House had passed a resolution seeking the use of Tamil in the Madras high court. The resolution was subsequently forwarded to the Union government.The latest proposal seeks to revive the demand and push for Tamil to be recognised as the principal language of the Madras high court.

Article Title: ‘No record’: Podcaster’s claim reignites row over CJP founder’s BU degree; Dipke hits back with video
Article Text:
A controversy has resurfaced regarding Abhijeet Dipke's educational credentials from Boston University

Sonam Wangchuk on Dipke’s political ambitions





NEW DELHI: A fresh controversy has erupted over Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke’s educational credentials after podcaster Prakhar Gupta said one of his friends who studied at Boston University could not find a record of Dipke’s graduation there.The claim was made during an episode of The Prakhar Gupta Xperience podcast featuring climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.Gupta said one of his close friends had studied at Boston University and had been actively involved in supporting the CJP-led protest at Jantar Mantar.“One of my best friends went to Boston University. It is also Abhijeet’s college,” Gupta said during the podcast.He said his friend had participated in the protests and produced media content in support of the movement.Gupta claimed that about a month later, his friend began looking into Dipke’s educational credentials and allegedly found no record of him graduating from Boston University.“He has gone down the rabbit hole of checking up Abhijeet’s education credentials and found there is no record of him graduating from Boston University,” Gupta said.Dipke, however, responded to the claim on X, appearing to mock the suggestion that his graduation could not be verified.“Not my fault that his friends were not invited at BU COM Grad events,” Dipke wrote, while sharing a video appearing to show him at an event associated with Boston University’s College of Communication graduate community.The video was a screen recording of a story posted by an Instagram account identified as “BU COM Grad, Student Council”.The latest allegation comes despite Boston University itself having published material identifying Dipke as a graduate.In a June 2026 article, Boston University’s College of Communication described Dipke as a “COM grad” and said he had completed his master’s in public relations from the university the previous year.The university article also carried an interview with Dipke in which he discussed how his studies at BU influenced the communication strategy behind the CJP campaign.Dipke has previously maintained that he studied at Boston University and earned a master’s degree in public relations. He has also said his education was financed through a Boston University scholarship and an education loan.Amid the controversy, Dipke had earlier said he was willing to produce his degree and other documents to establish his educational credentials.The dispute has now resurfaced as Dipke and the CJP leadership face increasing scrutiny over their backgrounds and political ambitions following the movement’s prolonged protests over examination-related issues.The same podcast also featured Wangchuk discussing Dipke and other CJP organisers, including their possible political ambitions.Wangchuk said he believed Dipke and his fellow organisers appeared to have political aspirations, although they had not explicitly told him about any such plans. He said there was nothing inherently wrong with political ambitions as long as the CJP remained a non-party platform.“Political ambition is very normal,” Wangchuk said, adding that he did not care about the organisers’ past political connections and had no problem with their present or future political aspirations.Wangchuk also said the organisers were not necessarily acting entirely selflessly and described them as “well meaning”, “quite skilled” and “above average”. He cautioned that their political aspirations should not turn the CJP platform itself into a vehicle for any political party.He said the organisers could eventually join an existing political party or form one of their own, but should preserve CJP as a “neutral, apolitical pressure group”.The comments came days before the Supreme Court quashed 127 FIRs filed against student protesters in five states in connection with the CJP agitation.Following assurances given before the court, CJP called off its proposed September 5 march from India Gate to Delhi Police headquarters.
Article Summary: A fresh controversy has erupted over Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's educational credentials. Podcaster Prakhar Gupta said one of his friends who studied at Boston University could not find a record of Dipke’s graduation there. The claim was made during an episode of The PrakHar Gupta Xperience podcast featuring climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Article Title: Nitin Gadkari urges all state governments to allow bike taxis; announces plan for negative points for traffic rule violations

NEW DELHI: Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari Wednesday urged all state govts to allow bike taxis, saying it could give employment to eight crore people.During the launch of a pilot programme — “Suraksha” — for on-the-spot free medical diagnosis and counselling for 10 lakh drivers, construction and high-risk workers involved in building highways and mines, he also said his ministry will amend Motor Vehicles Act to introduce a negative point system for drivers for traffic violations, which will result in suspension and cancellation of driving licence.The initiative will be implemented on 150-km covering Nagpur–Kamptee areas of NH-44 and mining belt in Chandrapur in Maharashtra, with a target of 10,000 people.Speaking about the programme, Gadkari sought better medical tests and healthcare for drivers and construction workers, saying that “health of our drivers is key for road safety and there is a dire need to focus on their eyecare and other health issues they face due to the nature of their work.”On the need to allow private two-wheelers, such as scooters and motorcycles, owners to allow transporting passengers, he said this will create employment opportunities in rural areas. “We have allowed this. But some states are not allowing this. Transport is a state subject. I will urge them to do so as this will give a source of livelihood to many,” Gadkari said.Highlighting the high number of deaths and violations of traffic and transport rules by drivers, the minister said that they have finalised the proposed legislation to penalise the “habitual offenders”. He said, “There will be negative points for each violation and accumulation of a certain point will result in suspension and even cancellation of licences. We hope this will instil responsible driving behaviour,” he said.

Article Title: Yasin Malik decides to divorce Pakistani wife Mushaal, denies any role in Sarla Bhat killing, seeks capital punishment for self
Article Text:
Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front chairman Yasin Malik

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front chairman Yasin Malik, in a 25-page affidavit filed on Wednesday before the additional sessions judge hearing Tada and Pota cases in Srinagar, has denied any role in the killing of Kashmiri Pandit nurse Sarla Bhat.In the affidavit, Malik also talks about divorcing his Pakistani wife Mushaal Malik to spare her the life of a widow and seeks capital punishment for himself. He says he will not contest the case.Malik, who has been in New Delhi’s Tihar jail since 2019, submitted the affidavit in response to the State Investigation Agency chargesheet regarding Kashmiri Pandit nurse Sarla Bhat, who was killed April 19, 1990, and in which Malik is arrayed as one of the accused. The affidavit was submitted to the court by Malik’s counsel, advocate Adil Pandit. The case is now listed for reply on Sept 19, 2026.“I have no complaint against this court or the prosecuting agencies. I respectfully state that, in my understanding, the present proceedings have arisen out of political circumstances and decisions and I believe that I have been falsely implicated in the present case,” Malik writes.Malik asks that his written submissions be read and treated as forming an integral part of this affidavit in evidence. On June 29, 2026, the SIA had filed a chargesheet in connection with the “tragic murder of Ms Sarla Bhat, a young Kashmiri Pandit woman who lost her life on 19 April 1990”, the affidavit reads. “To my utter shock and disbelief, I was arrayed as one of the accused in the said chargesheet after more than three decades of the occurrence,” Malik says.Malik says when the killing took place the administration of the erstwhile state of Jammu & Kashmir was headed by governor Jagmohan, known for personally scrutinising sensitive security files and maintaining close supervision over matters concerning militancy and public order, and at no point had Jagmohan suggested that he was involved in the case or was responsible for the killing of Kashmiri Pandits or their subsequent migration from the Valley.“During the relevant period in April 1990, I was critically injured, unconscious and undergoing medical treatment. The allegation that I ordered the killing of Ms Sarla Bhat out of revenge is, therefore, wholly false,” Malik claims in the affidavit. “It is, therefore, incomprehensible how a person who was unconscious, fighting for his own survival and widely believed to be dead, could have participated in, directed or orchestrated the commission of the offence alleged by prosecution,” he says.Malik addresses his wife Mushaal Malik and daughter Raziya Sultana, stating: “You (Mushaal) are twenty years younger than me, and I do not want you to spend the rest of your life carrying the burden of my circumstances or living as a widow. I therefore request you to find the courage to begin a new chapter of your life with dignity and hope… That, before I will be hanged, I have taken the decision to separate you from the bond of our nikah.“Considering my personal circumstances and after deep reflection, I have decided not to contest the trial proceedings further. My decision shall not be treated as an admission of any prosecution fact, guilt or acceptance of the allegations made against me. I request for capital punishment,” the affidavit reads.
Article Summary: Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front chairman Yasin Malik has denied any role in the killing of Kashmiri Pandit nurse Sarla Bhat. Malik also talks about divorcing his Pakistani wife Mushaal Malik to spare her the life of a widow. He says he will not contest the case.

GUWAHATI: Two Kuki-Zo MLAs travelled to Imphal Wednesday in defiance of a community whip and attended the Manipur assembly session in person for the first time since violence erupted in 2023, creating a hill-valley divide that is still to be bridged.Saikul legislator Kimneo Haokip Hangshing of Kuki Peoples' Alliance (KPA) and Independent MLA Haokholet Kipgen of Saitu, both in Kangpokpi district, chose to be in the assembly for the first day of the session despite Kuki Inpi Manipur's explicit instruction to stay away from Meitei-majority Imphal.Deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen and her BJP colleague, Henglep MLA Letzamang Haokip, attended the session over videoconferencing. Other four Kuki-Zo MLAs from BJP abstained. Manipur has nine Kuki-Zo MLAs, including two from KPA. Six of them had attended the budget session last Feb virtually.CM Y Khemchand Singh's office issued a statement lauding the two Kuki MLAs for making what it termed a "historic physical return" to the assembly. "Their attendance comes after a gap of three and a half years, during which representatives from the community had not physically participated in person in House proceedings," it said.Singh attributed the MLA duo's "positive step" to BJP-led govt's efforts to reduce the trust deficit among communities. "With collective efforts, Manipur can strive to walk the path to peace," Singh said.Kuki Inpi Manipur has barred elected community representatives from venturing into Imphal Valley until Union and state govts accede to their demand for a separate administration for the hills.While violence involving Kuki and Meitei communities has ebbed, Manipur is firefighting escalating tensions between Naga and Kuki groups in the hills, mainly along the Imphal-Tamenglong Road corridor in Kangpokpi. BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. Article Title: From Sushant Singh Rajput 'link' to CBI probe: The Disha Salian case so far
Article Text:
The Bombay High Court on Wednesday ordered a CBI investigation into Disha Salian’s death, citing concerns over the prolonged police probe and failure to register an FIR

What is the case?

What has the HC ordered?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sushant Singh Rajput 'link'

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe a CBI investigation is warranted in the Disha Salian case? Yes, definitely No, not necessary 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday ordered the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to register an FIR and take over the investigation into the death of Disha Salian, former manager of actor Sushant Singh Rajput , who died in June 2020.A bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale directed Mumbai Police to hand over all case records to the CBI and ordered that the probe be conducted by a suitably experienced and senior officer.The court also pulled up Mumbai Police over the manner and duration of its investigation, saying it had continued for about six years without an FIR being registered. The bench observed that the police investigation “raises more questions than it answers” and said a CBI probe was necessary.The 44-page judgment said there were “glaring discrepancies” in the police investigation and called for a “proper and substantive” probe.“In this case, we are of the opinion that the police had sufficient opportunity to investigate the offence, but they have not registered the FIR and have not carried out the investigation of a cognisable offence,” the court said.Reacting to the order, Salian’s father Satish Salian, who has pursued the case for six years and alleged that his daughter was murdered, said he felt “relieved” but had no reason to celebrate after losing his daughter.“I have been waiting for this for 6 years. There is no reason to be happy. I have lost my daughter. I feel relieved today. That's all,” he told reporters, adding that he had folded his hands and thanked the judge.Disha Salian was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai’s Malad area. Mumbai Police registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) and, after an inquiry, maintained that she had died by suicide.Salian’s father challenged the police’s handling of the case and approached the Bombay High Court, alleging that his daughter had been gang-raped and murdered.He also alleged a politically orchestrated cover-up to protect influential people and sought registration of an FIR and a CBI investigation, including into allegations against Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray.The high court, however, made it clear that it was not expressing any opinion on the allegations against any individual. It said the CBI would have to determine whether the evidence gathered during its investigation warranted treating anyone as an accused.The court pointed to several aspects of the investigation that it said required closer examination. One issue was the spot panchnama, or the record of the scene where Salian’s body was found, which the court noted had been conducted belatedly.The bench also questioned the absence of blood at the spot. It raised doubts about whether the injuries recorded in the case were consistent with a fall from such a height.“If the deceased had fallen on her face from the 12th floor, then it is difficult to accept that there was only one injury on the chin of the body. Not a single facial bone was fractured. We find this difficult to accept,” the court said, as quoted by PTI.During an earlier hearing, the court had also questioned how a fall from such height could result in such limited injuries. The prosecution had argued that Salian suffered severe facial, skull and rib fractures and that rain could have washed away blood from the spot. The court noted that the rain cited by the prosecution had occurred several hours after the incident.The bench also noted an apparent discrepancy concerning Salian’s clothing. It observed that while the panchnama and post-mortem report stated that her body had no clothes, photographs from the hospital and morgue appeared to show her wearing clothes.“There is room for reasonable doubt in all these aspects. However, we are not drawing any conclusion at this stage,” the court said.The court had also earlier questioned why Mumbai Police had registered only an ADR despite the allegations raised by Salian’s family. It noted that copies of the post-mortem report and ADR had not been provided to the family even years after her death.Salian’s lawyer Nilesh Ojha had alleged discrepancies in the post-mortem report and argued that an FIR should have been registered on the basis of the allegations and material placed before the authorities.The High Court directed the CBI to record Satish Salian’s statement and register an FIR. Mumbai Police was ordered to hand over all papers and records relating to the case to the central agency “forthwith”.The CBI has been asked to appoint a suitably experienced and senior officer to investigate the case.The court also imposed an important safeguard: no individual can be treated as an accused merely on the basis of the allegations made before the court.“Nobody shall be treated as an accused unless in the opinion of the investigating officer there are sufficient grounds to raise reasonable suspicion against him depending on the material collected during the investigation,” the court said.The bench also said that if the investigation finds that no criminal case is made out, the CBI must file an appropriate summary report before the competent court.“In case the investigation reveals that no case is made out, then the CBI shall file the appropriate summary report before the court concerned,” it said.Satish Salian will be free to challenge such a report and file objections before the court.The high court described Salian as an “unfortunate” father who had lost his young daughter in “tragic circumstances” and said the matter required a substantive investigation. At the same time, it refrained from commenting on the allegations made against specific individuals.Satish Salian’s petition sought an FIR and investigation into allegations against Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, son of former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray.The court however did not make any adverse finding against Thackeray and said it was for the investigating agency to examine the evidence.Thackeray had separately approached the high court seeking to intervene in the proceedings. In his application, he described Satish Salian’s petition as “false, frivolous and motivated” and sought an opportunity to be heard before any order was passed.The case has also drawn attention because Salian had briefly worked as a manager for actor Sushant Singh Rajput.Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian’s death. The proximity of the two deaths led to widespread speculation, although the cases were investigated separately.A CBI probe was also ordered into Rajput’s death. The agency subsequently filed a closure report stating that he died by suicide; the concerned court is yet to decide on the report.The latest order does not establish that Salian was murdered or that the allegations made by her family are true. It instead directs a fresh investigation by the CBI after finding that the police probe contained issues that, in the court’s view, warranted further examination.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court orders CBI to take over investigation into death of Disha Salian. Justices Sarang Kotwal and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale directed Mumbai Police to hand over all case records to the CBI. Salian’s father Satish Salian, who has pursued the case for six years and alleged that his daughter was murdered, said he felt “relieved” but had no reason to celebrate.

Article Title: 'A case of no probe', says Supreme Court, junks 25-yr-old murder case
Article Text:
Bihar Police’s case against six accused in 2001 firing case rejected by Supreme Court

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bihar police had proved its case before the trial court and Patna high court against six persons accused of firing indiscriminately to kill a man in broad daylight in 2001, but its evidence was trashed by the Supreme Court, which took more than a decade to acquit the accused by concluding that it was a case of "no investigation" having taken place.The snail-paced legal system saw one of the accused serving a life term awarded by the trial court and upheld by HC in 2015. The other five convicts had appealed against the HC decision. Acquitting them, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said, "There is complete lack of evidence in the present case, and testimonies (of eyewitnesses) do not inspire confidence." SC's remark that "the case is not of a faulty investigation but of no investigation having been carried out" indicates possible lack of judiciousness on the part of trial court or HC to separate grain from the chaff while appreciating evidence in the case. Otherwise, it is incomprehensible as to how the complete lack of evidence in the case, as pointed out by SC, had escaped the scrutiny of two judicial tiers.Justices Pardiwala and Chandran said it was aware that faulty investigation cannot be taken advantage of by the accused but added, "When there is no reliable evidence, merely because the IO was recalcitrant or a complaint of collusion was raised against him, the court cannot presume the guilt of the accused."SC said, "We are unable to find the prosecution having established the culpability of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. As we noticed, the eye-witness testimony does not inspire confidence, and there are no recoveries made or seizures effected as would have been done in a proper investigation."SC said the murder motive projected by the prosecution was sticky, an expert medical opinion went against the witness testimony on how the incident occurred, and there was no recovery of weapons or cartridges from the scene of crime in the case that saw witnesses claiming indiscriminate firing by the accused. Disbelieving the eye-witness account that the assailants came from behind and fired indiscriminately at the victim, who was walking, the bench said, "Expert evidence that there was an indication from the nature of the wound that the victim was sitting and that the firing was made from close quarters persuades us to disbelieve the eyewitness testimony. "
Article Summary: Bihar police had proved its case before the trial court and Patna high court against six persons accused of firing indiscriminately to kill a man in broad daylight in 2001. NEW DELHI: As two govt organisations took contradictory stands on commercial production of next-generation green firecrackers - with Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-NEERI approving new formulations and Central Pollution Control Board objecting - Centre Wednesday told Supreme Court that it intended to conduct fresh tests to assess the harmful impact of the use of barium.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Augustine George Masih that govt, after consulting stakeholders, had decided to conduct the tests in New Delhi, Bhopal, Kolkata and Chennai.Centre had asked CSIR-NEERI to develop green/low-emission fireworks - with particulate matter (PM) emission reduction of more than 50% - in association with manufacturers. Tamil Nadu Fireworks and Amorces Manufacturers' Association (Tanfama) devised new-generation formulation crackers with a reduced quantity of barium salts/nitrates in combination with other oxidisers.In a report, CSIR-NEERI said with the new formulations, emission reductions achieved for PM10 and PM2.5 were between 45% and 60%, and recommended that the formulations for light-emission fireworks (such as flowerpots, sparklers, chakkars, pencils, twinkling stars and their hybrids) be considered for commercial production.It also approved the manufacture of 'joined crackers', known as 'ladis', which have been banned by a court order.The report said there was a reduction in PM emissions by approximately 30% and a reduction in solid waste generation by up to 32% for joined crackers.CPCB asked how barium nitrate could be used in crackers when it was banned by SC. "This court, vide order dated Oct 23, 2018, has expressly banned the use of barium salts in firecrackers and, therefore, any formulation involving barium compounds, even in reduced quantities, is in contravention of the said order," it said in its communication to govt."The reported reduction in PM10 and PM2.5 levels has not been comparatively assessed with (i) improved low-emission crackers and (ii) green crackers formulated entirely without barium, rendering the claim incomplete and inconclusive," it added.The petitioners, on whose plea polluting firecrackers were banned, submitted that the court had over the years passed eight orders to ban the use of barium and its use in cracker manufacturing could not be allowed.SC asked Centre to get suggestions from experts, saying the court had no expertise in these matters.

TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT, NEPAL): India assured support for complete reconstruction of flood-ravaged Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur, two days after TOI reported that the institution was seeking New Delhi's help to rebuild on higher, safer ground.The assurance came less than a week after around 900 students on campus escaped the Aug 26 flash flood following an emergency evacuation, while hundreds more travelling to school were stopped from entering the danger zone. The school had 1,643 students enrolled.Indian ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava met the school's principal Rajendra Dawadi Tuesday. Srivastava recalled the institution's long association with India, including construction of its newer building through Indian grant assistance. He said Dawadi's timely action had saved lives of over 1,600 schoolchildren. TOI had earlier reported how around 900 students were inside the school when warnings came, while buses carrying hundreds of others were stopped before reaching the danger zone.Dawadi told TOI after the meeting with Srivastava on Wednesday: "We are deeply grateful to India for the reassurance and for standing with us at this difficult time.The assurance has given the entire school community hope at a time when we are trying to restart classes and also looking for a safe location for a permanent campus. Our entire school infrastructure has been destroyed, so our immediate priority is to bring the students back to classrooms. "The flood has swept away virtually the entire campus, including its 18-room, three-storey academic block. The school's two buses were among the few assets left. Two staffers - non-teaching employee Chulrim Lama and secondary teacher Santos Parihar - still remain missing.The school's links with India stretch back decades. Embassy of India records said Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School was established in 1951 and was designed by K I Singh, an Indian engineer who had come to Nepal for Trishuli Hydro Project. India later funded a new school building at a cost of NRs 25 million, or Nepalese Rs 2.5 crore, under India-Nepal Development Cooperation.Indian officials and local authorities inaugurated the building on Aug 2, 2022.India's latest assurance came as Nepal's private sector also mobilised assistance for schools and communities hit by the flood. Chaudhary Foundation, CSR arm of Chaudhary Group, announced immediate assistance to help Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School restart classes from a temporary location.Dawadi said restoring a Bailey bridge would make restart easier. He said bringing children back together with their classmates and teachers would help them recover from trauma.
Article Summary: India assured support for complete reconstruction of flood-ravaged Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur. Indian ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava met the school's principal Rajendra Dawadi Tuesday. The assurance came less than a week after around 900 students on campus escaped the Aug 26 flash flood.

SRINAGAR: Opposition BJP and governing National Conference (NC) held competing protest marches against each other in Srinagar Wednesday, with J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah accusing the UT administration of bias against NC protesters after they were blocked from heading to the BJP office.The BJP protest, starting from Lal Chowk, was similarly stopped from proceeding to Civil Secretariat.
