NEW DELHI: At least five people were killed and around 20 injured after a passenger bus collided with a bulker truck, on National Highway 39 near Badwar stand in Madhya Pradesh’s Rewa district on Wednesday.The collision sent the bus off the road and into a roadside ditch, district collector and district magistrate Narendra Kumar Suryavanshi told news agency ANI.“The collision between the bus and the other vehicle, a ‘capsule’ [tanker], occurred at a spot about 4 kilometres ahead of Gurh. In this incident, the bus fell into a roadside ditch. Immediately, the Superintendent of Police (SP), the entire administration, medical teams, local villagers, and public representatives reached the site. Everyone here worked with sensitivity during the rescue operation,” Suryavanshi told ANI.Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed grief over the accident and offered condolences to the families of those killed.“The loss of lives due to a mishap in Rewa, Madhya Pradesh is saddening. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. Praying for the swift recovery of the injured: PM,” the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) India said in a post on X.Giving a preliminary account of the casualties, the district magistrate said, “The rough estimate is that 20 people are injured and five have died. Everyone is engaged in the rescue operation.”The injured were being attended to as rescue operations continued at the crash site. Police and district administration officials were overseeing the response, with medical teams and local residents assisting in the rescue effort.Vice president CP Radhakrishnan also expressed condolences, saying, “Deeply saddened by the loss of precious lives in the tragic road accident in Rewa, Madhya Pradesh.“My heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and pray for strength and solace to them in this hour of grief. I also pray for the speedy recovery of those injured in the accident.”

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra on Wednesday slammed the party's rebel MPs for seeking additional time to respond to notices issued to them by the Lok Sabha secretariat.While talking to reporters, Mahua said that the rebel MPs' inability to respond within the stipulated period shows that they know they are in the wrong."We have filed 20 disqualification petitions against MPs who were elected on TMC tickets but joined hands with the BJP . The Lok Sabha Secretariat sent notices last week to them asking them to reply within seven days. The deadline is over, but they could not reply. Now they have sought another two-three weeks," Mahua said."We had written to the Lok Sabha Speaker in June. Why were they unable to reply in two months? Why does it take you more than one week to reply? If you ask me, I will not take so much time to reply," she added."The wigs and masks have come off. Their shamelessness and betrayal are for everyone to see," she said.This comes a day after TMC MP Sudip Bandhopadhyay said that the rebel MPs had sought an additional three weeks from the Lok Sabha secretariat to respond to notices issued on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification.Last month, the Lok Sabha secretariat had issued notices to the MPs after the Supreme Court agreed to hear Abhishek Banerjee's plea seeking an expeditious decision by Speaker Om Birla on the disqualification petitions.The rebel MPs are understood to be consulting lawyers before submitting their replies, with the additional time sought by them potentially extending the legal battle over their continuation as members of the House.The dispute is part of a larger political confrontation within the TMC following the party's defeat in the West Bengal assembly polls earlier this year, with the dissident camp challenging the authority of the leadership headed by party supremo Mamata Banerjee.The 20 Lok Sabha MPs subsequently aligned themselves with the NCPI and joined the BJP-led NDA, prompting the TMC leadership to initiate disqualification proceedings under the anti-defection law.

Article Title: Manipur assembly passes third resolution seeking NRC update before census
Article Text:

Shutdowns over demand for clear NRC roadmap

NEW DELHI: The Manipur Assembly on Wednesday adopted a resolution urging the Centre to update the National Register of Citizens (NRC) in the state before conducting the census exercise.This is the third such resolution adopted by the assembly since 2022.“The House once again reaffirms its previous resolution passed on August 5, 2022, and March 1, 2024, to urge the government of India to update the National Register of Citizens (NRC) in Manipur before conducting the census in the interests of the state in particular and the nation in general,” speaker Th Satyabrata Singh said.The resolution comes after the Centre deferred the census exercise in Manipur on Monday, a day before the house-listing exercise was scheduled to begin in the state.According to a statement issued by the chief minister's secretariat, the decision was taken after Union home minister Amit Shah chaired a high-level meeting in New Delhi to review the situation in Manipur.“The meeting agreed to defer the proposed Census exercise in the state considering the feelings and aspirations of the people of Manipur,” the statement said.The demand for implementing and updating the NRC has stemmed from apprehensions among sections of the Meitei and Naga communities that a census without the exercise could result in “demographic changes” in the state due to the alleged entry of illegal immigrants from neighbouring Myanmar, who have ethnic ties with the Kuki people.The Centre's decision to defer the census did not end protests over the demand for a clear roadmap on updating the NRC.Manipur's five valley districts witnessed a near-complete shutdown on Tuesday during a 24-hour general strike called by the Campaign for Just and Fair Delimitation.The organisation said the deferral of the census did not meet its main demand for a clear assurance that the NRC would be updated before any population enumeration.Meanwhile, a Kuki-Zo organisation questioned the Centre's decision to defer the census exercise, alleging that the matter had been decided while ignoring the voice of the community.
Article Summary: Manipur Assembly urges the Centre to update the National Register of Citizens (NRC) in the state before conducting the census exercise. The demand for implementing and updating the NRC has stemmed from apprehensions among sections of the Meitei and Naga communities that a census without the exercise could result in ‘demographic changes’

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar will travel to Ukraine and Poland from September 3 to 5, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday. The talks are expected to focus on bilateral ties, regional developments and issues of mutual interest.During the visit, Jaishankar will hold bilateral talks with Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha and Poland’s deputy prime minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski.The ministry's official release stated that the visit would focus on “enhancing bilateral relations” and provide an opportunity to exchange views on “regional developments and issues of mutual interest.”The Ukraine leg comes days after Ukraine’s first deputy head of the office of the president, Sergiy Kyslytsya, held what he described as a “substantive meeting” with India’s ambassador to Ukraine Anjani Kumar.In a post on X, Kyslytsya said they discussed “prospects for Ukraine-India relations, including India's role in efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine.”He said the meeting also covered Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent message to Russian President Vladimir Putin that “the time has come to move from an endless war to an end of war.”“We look forward to continued dialogue with India and to translating this shared interest in peace into concrete steps,” Kyslytsya said.The visit also follows the death of an Indian national in a Russian aerial attack on Ukraine. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said 12 people were killed in the assault, including the Indian citizen.“Overall, 12 people were killed, among them an Indian citizen, and dozens more were injured in the attack. My condolences to everyone who has lost family and loved ones,” Zelenskyy said.The Indian Embassy in Kyiv said it was in touch with the family and assisting with the early repatriation of the mortal remains.Jaishankar’s Poland visit comes ahead of an expected visit to India by Polish prime minister Donald Tusk. Poland’s ambassador to India Piotr Antoni Switalski said preparations were under way, describing the proposed visit as “the continuation of our political dialogue.”

Article Title: Ram temple trust gets three new trustees, brings in education, philanthropy and public life experience
Article Text:

LUCKNOW: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has appointed three new trustees, bringing into its governing body a philanthropist associated with the legacy of late VHP leader Ashok Singhal, a former public representative from Ayodhya and an educationist from Shikohabad whose family has links with the Indian Air Force, the RSS and the erstwhile Jana Sangh.The appointments of Mahesh Bhagchandka, Madan Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav were announced after the Trust’s meeting in Ayodhya on Wednesday. The three have filled vacancies in the Trust’s governing body.Mahesh Bhagchandka, 68, is founder-trustee of the Ashok Singhal Foundation, is related to Ashok Singhal, one of the prominent figures associated with the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Bhagchandka is also a graduate, businessman based in New Delhi. He is also the author of Hindutva ke Purodha, a book on prominent figures associated with the Hindutva movement.He participated in the rituals as a yajman during both the bhoomi pujan ceremony for the construction of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple and the temple’s pran pratishtha programme. His association with Ram-related cultural initiatives also includes work connected with the Shri Ram Van Gaman Yatra.Bhagchandka has been involved in the installation of Shri Ram Stambhs at 292 sacred sites associated with the route believed to have been taken by Lord Ram during his exile.He is also a member of the executive committee of the World Hindu Economic Forum.His appointment gives the Trust a member with experience in social and cultural initiatives as well as temple-related programmes. He is also related to late Vishwa Hindu Parishad leader Ashok Singhal and is a founder-trustee of the Ashok Singhal Foundation.Madan Mohan Pandey 74, is a law graduate and advocate based in Ayodhya Cantonment. He represented Shri Ram Lalla Virajman and late Mahant Ramchandra Paramhans Das in the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi legal dispute from 1990 to 2019 before the Allahabad High Court and the Supreme Court.His long association with the temple case places him among those who were directly involved in the legal proceedings that culminated in the Supreme Court judgment paving the way for the construction of the Ram temple at Ayodhya.Pandey also served as Uttar Pradesh’s additional advocate general for six years. Besides his legal practice, he is associated with religious and educational activities. He is the vice-president of the Shri Hari Satsang Samiti and the patron of the Kathakar Yojana training centre in Ayodhya.The third appointee, Nirmala Yadav, comes from a family with a long association with education and public life in Firozabad district. Though the family is originally linked to Uravar village under Sirsaganj tehsil, it has been settled in Shikohabad for several decades. Yadav herself originally hailed from Etah and moved to Shikohabad after her marriage.Yadav served as principal of BDM Girls PG College in Shikohabad from 1999 to 2006. She later became principal of Mahatma Gandhi Vidyalaya (PG) College in Firozabad and retired in 2022.Priyadarshini Upadhaya, the present principal of Mahatma Gandhi Vidyalaya and a former colleague of Yadav, described her as a highly capable administrator. She said Yadav had a strong command over institutional management and was particularly efficient in handling administrative and desk responsibilities.Yadav’s late husband, advocate Harendra Yadav, had served as an RSS district chief. Her father-in-law, Squadron Leader Surya Kumar Yadav, served in the Indian Air Force and was later associated with the Jan Sangh.According to her nephew Sachin Yadav, the family’s association with education dates back to 1916, when his great-grandfather, Chaudhary Shyam Singh Yadav, founded Kanhai College in Shikohabad. The family also produced a former MLA, Captain Nihal Singh and Squadron Leader Surya Kumar Yadav.
Article Summary: The appointments of Mahesh Bhagchandka, Madan Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav were announced after the Trust’s meeting in Ayodhya on Wednesday. The three have filled vacancies in the Trust's governing body. Yadav's family has links with the Indian Air Force, the RSS and the erstwhile Jana Sangh.

The post office passport seva kendra (POPSK) was inaugurated in Ladakh's Kargil on Wednesday to provide residents easier access to passport-related services, officials said.Minister of State for External Affairs and Environment, Forest and Climate Change Kirti Vardhan Singh inaugurated it in the presence of Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh V K Saxena and Member of Parliament Mohmad Haneefa Jan.The POPSK, established under a memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the Department of Posts and Passport Seva, is aimed at bringing citizen-centric passport services closer to people in the remote and geographically challenging region of Ladakh, they said.The facility will enable applicants to avail themselves of passport-related services closer to home, offering significant relief to residents who earlier had to travel to Srinagar or other distant centres for such services.The opening of the POPSK underscores efforts to leverage the extensive postal network for delivering essential citizen services, particularly in remote and underserved areas, they said.The initiative is expected to make passport services more accessible, efficient and people-friendly.The Ladakh Postal Division has added another milestone to its public-service infrastructure with the opening of the centre, an initiative led by Superintendent of Post Offices, Ladakh Postal Division, Arvind Kher, they said.
